title: Declaration and Payment of Dividend
outcomes: Explain the meaning and types of dividend.
Apply the sources and conditions for declaring dividend.
Apply interim dividend and payment rules.
Explain the Unpaid Dividend Account, IEPF and penalties for default.

meta.exam_tip: Keep the time chain clear: 5 days (deposit) → 30 days (payment) → 7 days (UDA) → 90 days (website) → 7 years (IEPF); 12% vs 18% interest.

concepts.title: Meaning and types of dividend
body: Section 2(35): dividend includes interim dividend. It is the portion of profits distributed to shareholders.
A final dividend is recommended by the Board and declared by members at the AGM; once declared it becomes a debt of the company. An interim dividend is declared by the Board between two AGMs.
Dividend is paid only in cash (including cheque, warrant or electronic mode) — but capitalising profits by issuing fully paid bonus shares or paying up unpaid amounts on shares is allowed.
concepts.analogy: Dividend is a share of profit paid in money.
concepts.work: Bonus shares are not dividend; they capitalise profits.

concepts.title: Sources of dividend and conditions (s. 123)
body: Section 123(1): dividend may be declared or paid only out of (a) profits of the current year after providing depreciation under Schedule II; (b) undistributed profits of earlier years after depreciation; (c) both; or (d) money provided by the Central or State Government for dividend under a guarantee.
A company may transfer such part of profits to reserves as it thinks fit before declaring dividend.
Before declaring dividend out of current profits, losses and arrears of depreciation of earlier years carried forward must be set off against the current profit (or the lower of the two).

Unrealised gains, notional gains and revaluation of assets, and changes in carrying amounts of assets or liabilities measured at fair value, are excluded from profits for dividend. Free reserves cannot be used except as the rules on inadequate profit allow (average rate, one-tenth cap, losses set off first, and remaining reserves condition).
No dividend can be declared by a company that has failed to comply with the deposit provisions of sections 73 and 74, as long as the failure continues.
concepts.analogy: Dividends come only from real profits, after old losses and depreciation are covered.
concepts.work: Revaluation surplus on land cannot fund a dividend.

concepts.title: Interim dividend and payment mechanics
body: The Board may declare interim dividend during a financial year or before the AGM, out of surplus in profit and loss and profits of the year up to the quarter preceding declaration.
If the company has incurred a loss in the current year up to the quarter-end just before the declaration, interim dividend cannot exceed the average rate of the three preceding years.
The dividend money (interim included) goes into a separate scheduled-bank account no later than five days after declaration, and paid only to the registered shareholder, to his order or his banker.
Dividend must be paid or warrants posted within thirty days of declaration.
concepts.analogy: Interim dividends are the Board's decision, but limited when the year looks weak.
concepts.work: A Board declaring interim dividend in November after losses in Q1 and Q2 must cap the rate at the three-year average.

concepts.title: Unpaid Dividend Account and IEPF (ss. 124–125)
body: Section 124: dividend declared but not paid or claimed within 30 days is transferred to an "Unpaid Dividend Account" in a scheduled bank within seven days after those 30 days.
The company prepares a statement of the names, addresses and unpaid amounts and places it on its website (and any website approved by the government) within ninety days of the transfer.
Default in transfer attracts interest at 12% per annum from the date of default, for the benefit of members.

Amounts in the Unpaid Dividend Account unpaid or unclaimed for seven years are transferred, with interest, to the Investor Education and Protection Fund (IEPF). Shares on which dividend has not been paid or claimed for seven consecutive years are also transferred to the IEPF; claimants may later reclaim them from the Fund.
Section 125: the IEPF is used to refund unclaimed amounts, promote investor education and awareness, and protect investors' interests.
concepts.analogy: Unclaimed dividend moves first to a special account and after seven years to the government fund.
concepts.work: A shareholder who forgot to claim dividends for eight years can still claim from the IEPF authority.

concepts.title: Right to dividend pending transfer and punishment (ss. 126–127)
body: Section 126: where a transfer of shares has been lodged but not registered, the dividend is transferred to the Unpaid Dividend Account (unless the registered holder authorises payment to the transferee), and rights or bonus shares are kept in abeyance.

Section 127: if a declared dividend is not paid or warrants not posted within 30 days, every director knowingly party to the default faces imprisonment up to two years and a fine of at least ₹1,000 for each day of default, and the company pays simple interest at 18% per annum during the default.

No offence arises where the dividend could not be paid because of operation of law, the shareholder's directions could not be complied with, there was a dispute about the right to receive it, it was lawfully adjusted against a sum due from the shareholder, or the failure was not due to the company's default.
concepts.analogy: Late dividend payment can mean jail for directors and interest for the company.
concepts.work: A dividend withheld because of a court order freezing the shares is not a default.

illustrations.title: Can the company pay this dividend?
illustrations.q: Divya Ltd. earned ₹42,00,000 this year after current depreciation. It carries forward a loss of ₹15,00,000 from earlier years and had not provided depreciation of ₹3,00,000 in an earlier year. The Board wants to declare equity dividend of ₹25,00,000 out of current profit. Advise.

solution.text: Since ₹24,00,000 is available, a dividend of ₹25,00,000 out of current profits is not permissible; the company may pay up to ₹24,00,000 (or use accumulated profits under the rules if conditions are met).

checks.label: Profit available for dividend after setting off past loss and arrear depreciation (₹)

illustrations.title: Late transfer to the Unpaid Dividend Account
illustrations.q: Kamal Ltd. declared a dividend on 10 August. ₹5,00,000 remained unpaid when the 30-day payment period ended, but the company transferred it to the Unpaid Dividend Account three months after the due date. What are the consequences?

solution.facts: Unpaid dividend not transferred within the time allowed; delay of three months.
solution.analysis: Unpaid or unclaimed dividend must be transferred to a special Unpaid Dividend Account in a scheduled bank within seven days from the end of the 30-day period. On default, the company pays interest at 12% per annum on the amount not transferred, from the date of default, and the interest goes to the members in proportion to the amount remaining unpaid.
solution.conclusion: Kamal Ltd. must pay interest of 15,000 (₹5,00,000 × 12% × 3/12) for the benefit of the members concerned, besides any penalty.

checks.label: Interest for 3 months' delay in transfer to UDA (₹)

jobs.title: Dividend compliance checklist
jobs.situation: A company has declared a final dividend at its AGM.
steps: Deposit the amount in a separate bank account within five days.
Move unpaid sums to the Unpaid Dividend Account within seven days after that.
Upload the unpaid list on the website within ninety days.
jobs.takeaway: Each step after declaration has its own deadline.

mcqs.q: Which is NOT a permitted source of dividend?
options: Money provided by government under a guarantee
mcqs.explain: Section 123 excludes unrealised gains and revaluation from profits available for dividend. The other three sources are expressly allowed. In practice: check the reserve composition.

mcqs.q: Before declaring dividend out of current profits, a company must set off:
options: Carried-forward losses and arrears of depreciation
mcqs.explain: Losses and depreciation not provided in earlier years, carried forward, must be set off against current profits before dividend. In practice: use the lower of the two amounts.
The Board may declare interim dividend during the year or before the AGM; final dividend is declared by members on the Board's recommendation. In practice: record the Board resolution.

mcqs.q: Dividend declared must be deposited in a separate bank account within:
mcqs.explain: Section 123(4) requires the dividend money to be placed in a separate scheduled-bank account no later than five days after declaration. Payment follows within thirty days. In practice: arrange funds beforehand.

mcqs.q: Unpaid dividend must be transferred to the Unpaid Dividend Account within:
options: 7 days after expiry of 30 days from declaration
mcqs.explain: Section 124 requires transfer of amounts unpaid or unclaimed within thirty days of declaration to the Unpaid Dividend Account within seven days after those thirty days. In practice: open the account in advance.

mcqs.q: Interest payable for delay in transferring to the Unpaid Dividend Account is:
mcqs.explain: Default in transfer to the Unpaid Dividend Account attracts interest at 12% per annum from the date of default, for the benefit of members. Delay in paying dividend itself attracts 18%. In practice: avoid both.

mcqs.q: Amounts in the Unpaid Dividend Account unclaimed for seven years go to:
options: The Investor Education and Protection Fund
mcqs.explain: After seven years, unpaid or unclaimed amounts, with interest, are transferred to the IEPF, along with shares on which dividends were unclaimed for seven consecutive years. In practice: send reminders before transfer.

mcqs.q: If dividend is not paid within 30 days, the company pays simple interest at:
mcqs.explain: Section 127 makes the company liable to pay simple interest at 18% per annum for the period of default, besides punishment of directors knowingly party to it. In practice: settle quickly.
mcqs.topic: Right to dividend pending transfer and punishment (ss. 126–127)

mcqs.q: A director knowingly party to failure to pay declared dividend is punishable with:
options: Imprisonment up to two years and fine of at least ₹1,000 per day
mcqs.explain: Section 127 prescribes imprisonment up to two years and a minimum fine of ₹1,000 for every day the default continues. In practice: directors must monitor payment.
mcqs.topic: Right to dividend pending transfer and punishment (ss. 126–127)

mcqs.q: No offence under section 127 arises when dividend is not paid because:
options: There is a dispute about the right to receive it
mcqs.explain: Exceptions include operation of law, shareholder's directions that cannot be complied with, disputes about entitlement, lawful adjustment against dues, and failure not due to the company's default. Lack of funds is not an exception. In practice: document the reason.
mcqs.topic: Right to dividend pending transfer and punishment (ss. 126–127)

summary: Dividend includes interim; payable in cash only.
Sources: profits after depreciation (current/past), government guarantee.
Set off past losses and arrear depreciation first; no unrealised gains.
Interim by Board; capped at 3-year average after interim losses.
Deposit 5 days; pay 30 days; UDA 7 days; 12% interest on delay in UDA transfer.
IEPF after 7 years; 18% interest and director punishment for non-payment.
remember: No dividend while deposit defaults continue.

viva.q: From what sources can dividend be paid?
viva.model: Current year profits after depreciation, undistributed profits of earlier years after depreciation, both, or money provided by government under a guarantee.

viva.q: Within how many days must dividend be paid?
viva.model: Within thirty days from the date of declaration.

viva.q: What is the Unpaid Dividend Account?
viva.model: A special account in a scheduled bank to which dividend unpaid or unclaimed within 30 days is transferred within the next seven days.

viva.q: What happens after seven years in the Unpaid Dividend Account?
viva.model: The amount with interest, and shares with dividends unclaimed for seven consecutive years, are transferred to the Investor Education and Protection Fund.

viva.q: What is the company's liability for late payment of dividend?
viva.model: Simple interest at 18% per annum for the period of default, besides punishment of directors.

cases.title: Shubham Ltd.
cases.case: Shubham Ltd. declared a final dividend on 15 September 2026, deposited the amount in a separate bank account on 25 September and posted warrants on 20 October. It also has a pending default in repaying public deposits.

mcqs.q: The deposit of dividend money on 25 September was:
options: Late, as it was due within five days
mcqs.explain: Section 123(4) requires deposit within five days of declaration, i.e. by 20 September; 25 September is late. In practice: arrange funds before the AGM.

options: Late, as the 30-day period ended on 15 October
mcqs.explain: Thirty days from declaration on 15 September ended on 15 October, so posting on 20 October breaches the time limit and attracts section 127, including 18% interest. In practice: plan dispatch early.
mcqs.topic: Right to dividend pending transfer and punishment (ss. 126–127)

mcqs.q: Given the deposit default, could Shubham Ltd. declare dividend at all?
options: No, while the failure under sections 73–74 continues
mcqs.explain: A company that has failed to comply with sections 73 and 74 on deposits cannot declare any dividend on equity shares as long as the failure continues. In practice: clear deposit defaults first.
